source.title: Analytic Study of Families of Spurious Minima in Two-Layer ReLU Neural Networks

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes a Gaussian-input teacher–student ReLU setting and reports that global and spurious minima have matching Hessian spectra to O(d^-1/2), challenging an explanation of generalization based exclusively on local curvature. It does not test the catalog's training/test generalization-gap versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports objective values at global and spurious minima and Hessian spectra, but no held-out test error or training/test generalization gap. The reported results do not test V1–V6 or V8. Hessian comparisons bear on V7's measured property, but the study does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or rank generalization gaps.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes population-loss minima and Hessian spectra in Gaussian-input teacher–student ReLU networks. It does not test any listed version. In particular, Hessian-spectrum similarity does not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or its correlation with training–test generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately captures the authors' curvature conclusion: the analyzed global and spurious minima have Hessian spectra agreeing up to O(d^-1/2), which they argue prevents local second-order curvature alone from explaining SGD's inductive bias in this setting. Their broader conclusion emphasizes symmetry-based analytic tools and preliminary evidence that increasing width turns spurious minima into saddles.
record.recipe_differences: Analytic study of the expected squared loss for finite two-layer ReLU networks with Gaussian inputs and planted realizable labels; studies minima and Hessian spectra rather than the claim's training/test error outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that changing hidden-neuron count in the over-parameterized regime can turn spurious minima into saddles; this is presented as preliminary experimental evidence and is outside the mapped claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 2 and Section 3 establish that the analyzed global and spurious minima have Hessian spectra agreeing up to O(d^-1/2), despite different population losses. This concerns local second-order curvature, without measuring magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the specified Gaussian teacher–student ReLU setting, Hessian spectra alone cannot distinguish the analyzed global and spurious minima to O(d^-1/2) accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: The conclusion reports preliminary experiments in which increasing student width at fixed input dimension turns families of spurious minima into saddles; their objective values appear constant. No test-error width sweep is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing student width can turn spurious minima into saddles in this teacher–student optimization problem.

record.problems: No held-out test-error or generalization-gap measurements; Hessian analysis is for the specified teacher–student Gaussian-input setting. The over-parameterization result is described as preliminary experiments, with a rigorous study deferred.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows: the reported objective values are training-objective landscape results, not training/test gap measurements; cited empirical generalization findings are prior work, not this study's results.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Image generalization of convolutional versus fully connected networks.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with training–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct V7 from tested_not_extracted to not tested. Equation (2) optimizes expected squared loss over the input distribution, so the reported objective values are population losses, rather than finite-sample training losses. Their omission is appropriate because they do not measure any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer held-out performance.
Large-batch training and held-out error under epoch budgets.
Tests Hessian-spectrum similarity for global versus spurious minima, but does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or correlate/rank it against the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Section 3 discusses flatness and generalization, but does not evaluate magnitude-aware perturbations or their correlation with training–test gaps.

tranche.reason: Analyzes population-loss minima and Hessian spectra, without testing any listed claim version. Neither the curvature analysis nor preliminary width experiments measure the generalization effects specified by V7 or V2.

source_check.notes: The authors' curvature conclusion is accurately represented: the analyzed spectra agree through O(d^-1/2), limiting explanations based exclusively on Hessian spectra. Increasing width turning spurious minima into saddles is preliminary optimization evidence, not a test-error result.
